paragraphs.text: Meeks and Abshire (2008) described prothrombin (factor II) deficiency as a rare autosomal recessive coagulation disorder that occurs in about 1 in 1 to 2 million people. Both hypoprothrombinemia and dysprothrombinemia have been described. Lancellotti and De Cristofaro (2009) distinguished 2 main phenotypes. Hypoprothrombinemia (type I deficiency) has low activity and low antigen levels together. Dysprothrombinemia (type II deficiency) has normal or near-normal synthesis of a dysfunctional protein. In some compound heterozygous cases, hypoprothrombinemia occurs together with dysprothrombinemia. Akhavan et al. (2000) described prothrombin deficiency as an autosomal recessive disorder with a moderately severe bleeding tendency. Lefkowitz et al. (2000) described dysprothrombinemia as a rare congenital cause of bleeding and noted that fewer than 25 families with a functional prothrombin defect had been reported.
